innovation_hypothesis: Read one 96-lane INT8 weight vector once, retain it in a held-weight register, and apply it to a bounded mask of neighboring FC1 contexts through F context accumulators. This trades cheap signed add/accumulate lanes for fixed weight bandwidth rather than widening SRAM reads.

scope.operators: the same ten exact-binary stage-0/1/2 FC1 modules and 100 M51-s10 payloads bound by M224
scope.stage3_policy: two non-binary FC1 modules remain conventional

semantics.K: maximum adjacent contexts in one row-bounded group
semantics.F: maximum contexts updated per service cycle for the held source weight
semantics.source_context_mask: exact residual-source presence across K contexts
semantics.service_cycles: sum over output blocks and unique sources of ceil(popcount(context_mask)/F)
semantics.weight_reads: one 768-bit weight-vector read per unique source and output block, independent of F and independent of held replay cycles
semantics.held_replay: if a source is active in more than F contexts, retain the same weight vector and serve the next context subset without another SRAM read
semantics.group_boundary: never crosses row, sample, module, timestep or batch boundary

resource_contract.accumulator_contexts: K independent signed Acc19 context banks

cycle_recurrence.serialized: weight DMA + current/candidate activation scan + choice metadata + chosen-parent seed + group descriptor + held-weight service + final commit

fairness.primary_reference: raw K1/F1 with the same 768-bit weight vector supply
